articles.body: The wave of populist energy propelling progressive Democrats to primary wins across the country reduced Wednesday morning to a ripple, just pushing Abdul El-Sayed to a narrow victory over his more moderate opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens. Francesca Hong will try to keep the progressive momentum alive in another swing-state test in Wisconsin next week. But if Hong, the democratic socialist frontrunner to claim her party’s gubernatorial nomination, wins her primary, she’s already recognizing the need to unite a broader coalition to win in November. “We absolutely need every single vote, and we’ll be fighting to earn every single vote,” Hong said in an exclusive interview with POLITICO on Wednesday morning. “I’ve talked to moderates and independents, Republicans, folks who don’t have a political home right now, and they have a lot of concerns about what's going on in the state. They also have concerns about things I've said in the past,” she added. “But what we’re focusing on is how to come together to actually deliver for Wisconsinites, and that’s going to be electing Democrats down and up the ballot this cycle.” Hong, a state Assembly member and former restaurant owner, this week faced criticism from across the political spectrum about a slew of old social media posts espousing far-left views, from declarations to abolish the police to a call to “cancel Thanksgiving.” And El-Sayed’s knife-edge win right next door is reigniting concerns among some Democrats that a battleground may not be ready for such a lefty leader. Hong appears to be moderating on — or at least adding context to — some of her more controversial positions. She has walked back her stance on police abolition while emphasizing the need to better tackle the underlying causes of crime. She told POLITICO many of her old posts were “jokes,” including the one about Thanksgiving, which she said is actually her favorite holiday. Still, Hong isn’t giving up her democratic socialist bonafides. “The vision that we have for Wisconsin is one that my local DSA chapter shares,” she said, adding that “we’re fighting to make sure that we're building the diverse coalition that we need to make sure that we win this for Wisconsinites in November.” Hong has notched endorsements from several national progressives, including Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) and Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), who rallied alongside her and the progressive podcaster Hasan Piker last weekend. But she hasn’t been endorsed by the country’s two most prominent democratic socialists and standardbearers of the progressive movement: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.). Hong told POLITICO she has not spoken to either and attributed their lack of endorsement to their focus on federal races — though Sanders endorsed Troy Jackson in the Vermont governor’s race before he lost and became the Senate nominee, and both endorsed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani last year. “We have been focusing on winning a Democratic primary and staying above the drama,” Hong said. Despite a major fundraising disadvantage, Hong has emerged as an unlikely frontrunner. She has led in the polls for months and became the all-but-presumed nominee after her main opponents, Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes and Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez , both dropped out amid simmering scandals that embroiled their campaigns. Hong’s chief primary opponent next week is Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who dropped out of the race then jumped back in last month and has the endorsement of the state’s current Gov. Tony Evers, a moderate Democrat. Whoever wins on Tuesday will face off against the President Donald Trump-endorsed GOP Rep. Tom Tiffany. Hong believes her lead is due to a grassroots campaign that has excited Democratic primary voters in Wisconsin. “Free child care, fully funding our schools, taxing the billionaires and a moratorium on AI data centers is what the majority of Wisconsinites have been telling us that they want, and we are the campaign that is listening,” she said in the interview. The Crowley campaign is pointing to the Michigan results as a sign that they can still catch Hong. “There is still a long way to go in this race,” Crowley spokesperson Eddie Vale said. “If you can't handle an easy CNN interview about Thanksgiving how can you possibly face the full wrath of the Republican attack machine?” To beat Tiffany in the general, Hong would likely need to pick up support from more moderate Democrats and independents — all while dodging a deluge of Republican attacks digging up her old comments and seeking to paint her as “woke.” “All Francesca Hong has to offer Wisconsin is bigger government, a plan to make Wisconsin the highest-taxed state in the nation, and a record of calling to abolish the police and prisons,” Tiffany said in a statement to POLITICO. “They are trying to get a head start on labeling her ahead of the primary because they don't see the result changing,” said Winnebago County Executive Gordon Hintz, who was minority leader in the state Assembly when Hong was first elected. “There’s a very big discussion going on in Wisconsin, much as there was in Michigan, about whether a very progressive candidate can prevail in the primary and in the general election,” said John Nichols, a Madison native who wrote an anti-capitalist manifesto with Sanders. “It goes to a lot of questions about what's been said in the past and how much people care.” Asked if she planned to change her messaging strategy ahead of the primary, Hong flipped the question back to Tiffany. “When it comes to tailoring messaging, it's important to recognize that what we have to offer are actual solutions, and what Tom Tiffany is bringing are clearly more Trump tariffs,” she said. Tiffany, in his statement, hit back. “While she focuses on promoting socialism, defending inflammatory statements, and campaigning alongside terrorist sympathizers, I'll remain focused on ending the 400-year property tax hike, rooting out fraud, bringing good-paying jobs back to Wisconsin, and making life more affordable after eight years under a Democrat governor,” he said. Like this content? Consider signing up for POLITICO's Playbook newsletter .
articles.headline: The democratic socialist facing swing-state realities — and her old tweets

articles.body: President Donald Trump’s most vocal opponents on the right were sowing the seeds for a future third-party political organization during a weekend get-together aimed at undercutting the Republican establishment. The meeting at Tucker Carlson’s compound in Maine with Rep. Thomas Massie, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene and others — captured in a photo posted by Greene on Saturday — served as a launch pad for a possible independent presidential campaign focused on unwinding U.S. involvement in foreign conflicts. “We said no more foreign wars and we meant it and supported Donald Trump because he made that promise. But he’s betrayed us all,” Greene wrote in the post. “The movement has begun.” Joe Kent, the former Trump national security official who resigned earlier this year and attended the weekend confab with Carlson, said the group congregated to strategize on how to best organize their shared opposition to the war in Iran. “There's a lot more nuts-and-bolts work that needs to be done there,” Kent said in an interview on “The Young Turks,” the progressive talk show. “Running as a third-party candidate is challenging. Not impossible, but it is very challenging. But that's kind of the consensus that we came to, that the current system just simply doesn't work, and we have to find something new to save our country.” Carlson, Greene and Massie all backed Trump ahead of the 2024 election. But each one broke with Trump over the course of his second term as the Trump administration continued to coordinate military operations with Israel in the Middle East. Greene and Massie were also loudly critical of Trump’s opposition to releasing federal investigative documents relating to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, further drawing Trump’s ire. It’s unclear who would lead the newborn movement. Kent said every attendee at the Maine meeting urged Carlson to run for president in 2028 with their group’s backing but noted that Carlson said he wouldn’t run. “Hopefully he wakes up one day and Tucker says he's going to run,” Kent said. Carlson and Massie did not respond to requests for comment. Greene declined to comment. The challenges facing third-party and independent presidential candidates are enormous. They must navigate different signature requirements and deadlines in each state just to get on the ballot. Past independent campaigns have been unable to compete financially with the two major parties. The most recent third-party presidential campaign — Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s independent bid in 2024 — ended months before Election Day when Kennedy endorsed Trump. At the time he dropped out, Kennedy was polling in single digits and fighting lawsuits seeking to block him from the ballot in multiple states. Kent said the policy platform for the group’s hypothetical third-party campaign in 2028 would ignore most domestic matters and further emphasize their staunch anti-interventionism. “I think it is having a very, very simple platform, and it's acknowledging upfront, like, we are going to disagree on a lot of domestic policy and a lot of social issues,” Kent said. “At the end of the day, the president can talk a lot about all those things, but he really doesn't have a lot of power.” “We do agree that we don't want Israel dictating our foreign policy,” he added. “We don't want any more foreign wars.” Carlson didn't signal his involvement in any broader political project or back a third-party candidate for 2028 during his show Wednesday. Instead, he delivered an hour-long monologue laying out his worldview and aspirations for the country. His vision covered familiar territory — including encouraging Americans to have more children, ending immigration and promoting healthy foods. In addition to denouncing Trump, he called Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth a "deranged, bloodthirsty monkey," for his conduct during the Iran War. Lisa Kashinsky, Alec Hernandez and Sam Benson contributed to this story.
articles.headline: Anti-Trump conservatives Tucker Carlson, MTG, Massie huddle about launching third-party movement

articles.body: Abdul El-Sayed has just three months to convince a fractured Democratic Party to unite behind him after a nasty primary. Even before his narrow win over moderate Rep. Haley Stevens became official Wednesday , El-Sayed had begun the difficult process of trying to patch things up with a moderate wing of the party he’d spent months flaying as corporatist stooges as Republicans launched their first wave of attacks of the general election. He says he looks forward to “building relationships” with Jewish voters. And some top Democrats in Michigan and Washington alike are largely filing behind him in a show of unity ahead of November’s high-stakes election. “To all of our supporters here tonight, watching on TV, tomorrow we begin to mend fences,” El-Sayed told a crowd of supporters early Wednesday before the race was called, asking them to show “magnanimity in victory.” “We need to move forward and start bringing this party together,” El-Sayed reiterated on MS NOW’s Morning Joe hours later. And, in a speech formalizing his victory after it was called at 10 a.m. Eastern, he said: “Whatever differences that we might have had in the primary, they pale in comparison to what unifies us.” El-Sayed has little time to force a reconciliation before he faces off against Mike Rogers, a Donald Trump-endorsed former representative with the backing of Washington’s GOP Senate apparatus. Michigan is one of the nation’s top battlegrounds, a state Trump has won twice but where Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin narrowly defeated Rogers in 2024. Early voting begins in five weeks. Already prominent Michigan Democrats like Slotkin and Rep. Debbie Dingell are working to consolidate support behind El-Sayed, showing efforts from both the moderate and progressive flanks after a bitter primary that put tensions over Israel and campaign finance in the spotlight. “We do have to unite,” Dingell said in an interview. “Abdul’s got to figure out how he's going to bring people that were part of Haley's coalition and have them know that he cares about the values that they have, which I know he does, but he's got to talk to them. This coalition has got to be a very broad coalition.” Michigan Democrats plan to hold their so-called post-primary “unity breakfast” Thursday morning in Southfield, where they will rally behind party nominees. The contest was separated by less than a percentage point when the AP called the race Wednesday morning. Stevens immediately conceded and called for unity. And state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who dropped her U.S. Senate bid a month before the primary, had already endorsed El-Sayed, saying she wanted to enter November “as a unified party” after “a brutal primary.” “We must elect Democrats up and down the ballot,” Stevens said in a statement Wednesday, promising her support to El-Sayed after calling her primary with him “a thorough and rigorous campaign that brought out the full span of views within the Democratic Party.” The primary was animated by charges of sexism, racism and religious bigotry. Splits over Israel played prominently in the race: El-Sayed attacked Stevens incessantly for relying on outside spending from groups like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which spent a record $32 million on her behalf. In the race’s final days, Stevens and her allies accused El-Sayed of antisemitism and sexism , and El-Sayed’s allies accused Stevens of Islamophobia . Outgoing Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.), who had endorsed Stevens, said he spoke with El-Sayed Wednesday morning and congratulated him. He said he will “work hard to make sure” Democrats coalesce behind El-Sayed. “The party has to all come together right now,” he told POLITICO. “We don't have a lot of time, but everybody has to come together and understand that as Democrats, whatever differences we have between us as Democrats are minor compared to the differences between our Democratic candidate and the Republican candidate.” Republicans are already plastering the airwaves with their preferred attack: Painting El-Sayed as “radical” and “dangerous” while emphasizing the full name of the American-born son of Egyptian immigrants. “Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, the most radical Senate candidate in America,” a new National Republican Senatorial Committee ad says . “Abdul El-Sayed: Dangerously radical,” says a new Senate Leadership Fund ad. In a statement Wednesday morning, Rogers called El-Sayed an "extremist” who “campaigns with people who refuse to condemn terrorism” — likely a reference to comments made by his ally, far-left streamer Hasan Piker , which Piker has since said he regretted. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice,” said Rogers, a former FBI special agent. “Never in a million years did I think that I would be running against someone who believes America deserved 9/11.” Cullen Schwarz, a longtime Democratic strategist in Michigan, said Democrats need to portray Rogers as the extreme one if they’re going to emerge victorious in the must-win Senate race. “As Democrats move forward, I hope we remember that in politics, the real battle is over moving the Overton window,” he said. “The Republicans are going to try to paint progressives across the country as extreme. It's extreme to support Donald Trump.” If that is the frame, Schwarz said, he doesn’t think Democrats will have any issues reunifying. “Democrats will immediately remember the fight we're facing in the fall,” he said. “There's been no force more unifying for Democrats than Donald Trump,” El-Sayed could have the most work to do in rural, working-class areas and among Black voters. He won just 34 percent of the vote in Detroit, according to unofficial returns. And Stevens won a majority of votes across counties where less than 30 percent of adults have a college degree, according to a POLITICO analysis. Matt Duss, a former foreign policy adviser to Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), said Democrats — from Michigan to Washington — need to line up behind El-Sayed. “Frankly, the Democratic establishment needs to very quickly consolidate around him — all of them,” said Duss, executive vice president at Center for International Policy. “If they believe what they say about needing to take Michigan for Democrats in the Senate, they can show us by getting all in behind El-Sayed right now.” El-Sayed’s emergence from the contentious primary — which saw record levels of outside spending in one of the nation’s key battlegrounds — will require some Washington Democrats who previously kept him at arm’s length to now embrace him. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.). said he preferred Stevens in the primary, but he released a statement Wednesday saying he and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand “look forward to working with Abdul and Democrats across Michigan to win this seat in November.” And the narrow result is forcing progressives who had been expecting a dominant, double-digit victory to recalibrate their expectations as their attention shifts to the general. “Tough result for Democrats,” said Adrian Hemond, founder of a Michigan-based bipartisan advocacy and outreach firm. “The promised populist wave was a dud… If you think the primary was nasty, just wait until next week. General election voters are less college educated and less ideological, so they have to find a way to sell ideology to normal people.” Jessica Piper, Adam Wren, Ali Bianco and Mia McCarthy contributed reporting.
articles.headline: Messy Michigan primary leaves Democrats licking wounds

articles.body: President Donald Trump’s endorsed candidate lost a top battleground Republican primary in Michigan — to a candidate who suspended his campaign last month. Amir Hassan, a Navy veteran and former law enforcement officer from Flint backed by Trump, finished significantly behind Tom Smith on Wednesday. Hassan rallied with Trump in Milford, Michigan, just last week. Smith, a retired engineer, had dropped out in mid-July and endorsed another candidate who ended up in third in the primary. Smith told POLITICO that he would now return to challenge first-term Democratic Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet for the purple 8th District. “I look forward to working with Speaker [Mike] Johnson and the entire Republican team to expand our House majority and advance President Trump’s America First agenda to lower costs for working families and make America affordable again,” Smith said in a statement. McDonald Rivet is among the more than a dozen Democratic incumbents seeking reelection in a district Trump won in 2024. But a GOP strategist, granted anonymity to speak candidly, characterized her as a “powerhouse.” The strategist added that Hassan had “clear flaws as a candidate” and the “GOP base was reluctant to support a dude named Amir Hassan.” A handful of Trump-endorsed candidates have lost state-level races this year — including the governor’s races in Iowa and Georgia — but Hassan is the first congressional candidate to lose despite the president’s support this cycle.
articles.headline: Trump-backed candidate in battleground Michigan district loses to opponent who dropped out

articles.body: Michigan Rep. Shri Thanedar lost his primary to democratic socialist Donavan McKinney on Wednesday — the latest victory for progressives who’ve been on a hot streak of ousting incumbents in safe-blue districts. Thanedar’s 13th District was a top priority for groups like Justice Democrats that are committed to primarying incumbent members that they believe aren’t in line with the areas they represent. Justice Democrats helped recruit McKinney into the race and spent nearly $1 million on his behalf, making his campaign one of its biggest targets this cycle. McKinney, a state representative, had secured the backing of a number of progressive House Democrats, including some members of the Congressional Black Caucus who bucked party leadership, which was standing behind Thanedar in the heavily Black Detroit-based district. Some of Thanedar’s colleagues were also frustrated by his efforts to force a vote on impeaching President Donald Trump last year, an effort he ultimately backed away from . The district is a safe seat for Democrats, and McKinney is expected to win easily in November.
articles.headline: Thanedar becomes latest incumbent to fall to a progressive challenger

articles.body: Abdul El-Sayed is Democrats’ Senate nominee in Michigan, a seismic victory for progressives that carries massive implications for both the Senate battlemap and the Democratic Party’s future. The progressive former public health official on Wednesday narrowly defeated establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens, who was boosted by a record-breaking $32 million in spending from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. His margin was far slimmer than progressives had anticipated based on polling that had shown him with a double-digit lead ahead of the election, blunting what they hoped would be an emphatic capstone to a series of high-profile wins that had tilted the party’s ideological civil war in their favor. El-Sayed will have to work overtime to convince skeptical centrists that a progressive can win in purple territory against former GOP Rep. Mike Rogers in a critical battleground that will decide Senate control. His victory comes after a contentious primary that was defined by clashes over everything from Israel to immigration to health care. Stevens and her allies lobbied accusations of sexism and antisemitism against El-Sayed, whose supporters in turn accused the moderate Democrat of Islamophobia. Wednesday’s result is a setback for the pro-Israel lobby as well as for leaders within the Democratic establishment — most notably Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer — who had thrown their weight behind Stevens. El-Sayed’s win has the potential to scramble Schumer’s gameplan for November; Democrats need to keep retiring Sen. Gary Peters’ seat if they have any hope of retaking the chamber. And it’s emboldening Republicans who hold a cash advantage heading into November and are growing bullish about their chances for a flip against a progressive who was their preferred nominee. State Republican Party Chair Jim Runestad said the GOP plans to paint him as a “far-left democratic socialist.” Jason Roe, a longtime Republican operative in Michigan, previously told POLITICO that “El-Sayed is not doing very well outstate and I think that’s what a lot of Republicans are banking on. It will be very difficult for him to beat Rogers with those rural counties.” Still, El-Sayed’s emergence from the bruising primary that became ground zero for Democrats’ ideological war stands as progressives’ biggest win yet in a year when the left has harnessed a wave of anti-establishment angst to deliver a series of stunning upsets. And it carries significant implications for how Democrats will approach a state that will have an outsized role in picking the party’s next presidential nominee in 2028. El-Sayed has sought to position his win as a springboard for growing progressives’ influence ahead of 2028 .
articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary — a major victory for progressives

articles.body: South Dakota Democratic Senate nominee Julian Beaudion dropped out of the race Tuesday, a move that comes following heightened pressure from within the party to clear the way for a stronger independent candidate, according to paperwork filed with the South Dakota Secretary of State’s office . Beaudion’s decision comes on the same day as the deadline to withdraw, and just days after he told POLITICO he was not going to leave the race. Now, independent Brian Bengs will face a one-on-one battle with Republican Sen. Mike Rounds in November. In a statement, Beaudion likened his decision to the failed Apollo 13 mission to the moon. “It is with a tremendous amount of gratitude to everyone who has supported our campaign mission and a great amount of sorrow, that I say, ‘Houston, we have a problem,’” he wrote. Beaudion is the third Democrat in a deep-red Senate race who has left in order to give independents — who have polled better and raised more money — a better shot at defeating Republicans. Already, Democrats in Idaho and Nebraska have dropped out and endorsed independents. But Montana Democrat Alani Bankhead has steadfastly insisted she will not suspend her campaign for the better-funded independent Seth Bodnar in what otherwise could be the best shot for an independent candidate to knock off a red-state Republican this fall. Bengs, a former Democrat who was crushed by Majority Leader John Thune when he ran for Senate in 2022, has touted internal polling showing a competitive race with Rounds — but only if Beaudion exited.
articles.headline: South Dakota Democrat exits Senate race, clears way for independent

articles.body: The battle to become the country’s next progressive leader in the mold of Bernie Sanders is heating up ahead of Democrats’ direction-defining Michigan Senate primary. Nowhere is the jockeying and strategy unfolding behind the scenes more pronounced than between Democratic Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and Ro Khanna of California, who have taken disparate approaches to the midterms as they build out their political brands. Khanna’s go-everywhere mentality versus Ocasio-Cortez’s more selective involvement in key races this cycle will test their political acumen and relationships, potentially setting them up for a 2028 presidential race that could decide who will inherit the movement. In much of Sanders’ inner circle, who comes next is pretty obvious, even as the wider progressive movement continues to clash over the answer. “It’s always been clear that AOC is the heir,” one person close to Sanders who’s been involved in such conversations with him for years, granted anonymity to share their understanding of the private discussions. “Always.” Yet within the broader Sanders coalition, there is plenty of behind-the-scenes posturing — and outright bickering — over who will ultimately take over for the Vermont senator. Khanna’s allies say Ocasio-Cortez is playing it too safe to be the next standard-bearer, with some prominent left-wing leaders irked by her sparing endorsement strategy. Ocasio-Cortez’s and Khanna’s diverging paths are on full display in Michigan , where Democrats’ most contentious Senate primary is coming to a head Tuesday in a critical battleground that will have outsized importance in selecting Democrats’ next presidential nominee. Both representatives and Sanders have backed Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official who has surged in polls against establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens as he consolidates support among the left. But only Ocasio-Cortez has appeared alongside Sanders in stumping for El-Sayed, with the two holding a joint rally in Lansing, Michigan, last month. Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders are featured prominently in one of El-Sayed’s closing television ads, in a key sign of who the campaign thinks can best help push him over the finish line. Khanna, meanwhile, cut a separate digital fundraising appeal for El-Sayed and has campaigned for him without Sanders. Sanders and Khanna do maintain a relationship — the California representative was a national co-chair of Sanders’ 2020 presidential bid — but there’s doubt within the Vermont independent’s orbit over how successful a Khanna presidential run would be or whether he's best positioned to inherit the progressive throne, should Ocasio-Cortez choose not to run for president in 2028. "Ro is basically already running, but not many are taking him too seriously as the movement's next leader," said another operative close to Sanders, granted anonymity to speak candidly. In an interview, Khanna brushed off the notion that there's a single heir to the Vermont senator’s progressive movement. "I believe that Sanders is going to have many successors over decades, and the key is to build a majoritarian progressivism that can win across the country," he said. Asked whether an Ocasio-Cortez presidential bid would change his calculus, he answered flatly: "No." His decision, he says, will come “around Thanksgiving.” A representative for Ocasio-Cortez declined to comment. Sanders, for his part, is trying to rise above the jockeying. “The presidential election is in 2 years and 3 months,” Sanders said in a statement. “Let’s focus now on how we resolve the urgent issues facing our country. There is plenty of time to worry about possible presidential candidates.” Why Sanders world sees AOC as the successor Sanders, 84, and Ocasio-Cortez, 36, share a deeply personal bond their advisers say transcends politics but remains rooted in their shared ideals. They talk directly about key policy, political ideas and candidates to boost, and they even coordinated their endorsements around a group of New York democratic socialists and progressives who ultimately won House seats. The two also share a circle of advisers, including Faiz Shakir and Mike Casca. Casca, a former long-time Sanders aide, now serves as Ocasio-Cortez’s chief of staff and plays a major role in shaping policy and political strategy. Shakir is an adviser to Sanders and executive director of More Perfect Union, a progressive nonprofit media organization. “I’m sure there are a lot of people who are interested in being the next Bernie Sanders, I think he’d be less inclined to give them his endorsement” over Ocasio-Cortez, said a third person close to Sanders, who’s been involved in the conversations around his political and policy strategy for years, granted anonymity to discuss them. Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez have approached the midterms differently. The Vermont independent has worked to expand his endorsement roster and his presence on the campaign trail this year, which his allies see as an effort to cultivate a lasting generation of progressive leaders to carry on his movement. He often endorses early, acting as a validator for left-leaning candidates’ campaigns and platforms, while Ocasio-Cortez has been serving as more of a closer. It’s a strategic shift for the New York Democrat, who used to get involved in races earlier — a calculus advisers say is a recognition of her ability to mobilize certain voting blocs, like communities of color and working-class voters, late in the game. They don’t coordinate on every contest, but they have joined forces in several races — including El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate race and Sam Forstag’s House primary in Montana. Ocasio-Cortez called Sanders as soon as she decided to endorse El-Sayed and they immediately began planning a rally for him, according to a person familiar with the discussions and granted anonymity to describe the private conversations. Earlier this year, Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez together also developed the leading progressive push to address artificial intelligence. Sanders was the first member of Congress to call for an AI moratorium, and he helped shape Ocasio-Cortez’s stance. The pair unveiled joint legislation in March to ban the rapid build up of data center construction. Months later, the issue is now cutting across progressive and conservative voting blocs, is a preeminent policy issue on Capitol Hill and is at the heart of dozens of midterm races and even early 2028 presidential talk. “Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and I understand what is at stake,” Sanders said as he introduced the AI moratorium bill alongside the New York Democrat this spring in the Senate. Progressive candidates whose campaigns have received nods from both Ocasio-Cortez and Khanna say they are both key validators who carry different appeal. Khanna has risen in prominence because of his push to release files on Jeffrey Epstein. And Ocasio-Cortez brings the kind of star power and nationalized spotlight that campaigns say is invaluable for growing candidates’ exposure, particularly among younger progressive voters who can be trickier to turn out. “AOC’s very popular, she has a lot of grassroots support … all across the country,” said Adam Hamawy, who was endorsed by both representatives in his New Jersey House primary this spring. “Ro Khanna has not just progressives, but he’s had a strong stance against corruption. … There’s a lot of overlap but each of them have specific things that come together to paint a wider picture than if I just had one.” Don’t count Ro out yet Not everyone around Sanders is sold on Ocasio-Cortez as the heir apparent. Khanna allies argue he's the one who has been putting in the work — and sticking his neck out for the progressive movement — by backing primary challengers to incumbents, getting out front on issues like the Epstein files, and recently traveling to the West Bank. “People who are supporting her are supporting her more as a brand," said one Khanna ally and Sanders world operative, granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. "What does it mean to work with her? What does it mean for her to pass a bill? I don't know her theory of change." There is fear Ocasio-Cortez is "weirdly isolating herself" over the years ahead of a 2028 decision, the operative added. "I could not tell you who AOC's advisers are at this point [beyond Casca]. If you're thinking of running for president, you want to be in an expansive, elevated, exciting space, not in a controlled environment.” Ocasio-Cortez has been significantly more selective in her endorsements than either Khanna or Sanders, backing left-wing candidates across several competitive House primaries but steering clear of some of the messiest contests on the map, including Maine Senate and Wisconsin’s imploding gubernatorial primary. That approach has drawn consternation from some on the left who say she’s playing it too safe given her political cachet, particularly as she declines to join other progressives in endorsing against incumbents — notably in her own backyard — even though that’s how she won her seat in 2018. “Who cares about your win-loss ratio? What I care about is, are you trying to help fellow progressives or aren’t you?” said Cenk Uygur, a Khanna supporter who founded the progressive online network “The Young Turks” and Justice Democrats. “AOC cares so much about her colleagues, and her colleagues are establishment Democrats. I don’t care about them. In fact, I’m opposed to them,” Uygur added. “I want them challenged in primaries.” Khanna has worked to keep his own close ties to Sanders and his circle. Jeff Weaver, Sanders’ 2016 campaign manager, now serves as a senior adviser to Khanna as he’s pushing to be a high-profile progressive leader and laying the framework for a possible 2028 presidential run. “No two candidates are equal,” Weaver said. “But I think Ro Khanna has the chance to do what Bernie did, which is to have appeal beyond the Democratic base.” Khanna has spent years trying to build the kind of early-state infrastructure a presidential campaign requires, traveling to early primary and battleground states to lay the organizational groundwork for a potential run. Since 2021, he has been working to assemble steering committees of 75 to 100 people in New Hampshire and Nevada, with another being built in South Carolina, while working with local political power players, according to Shannon Jackson, another longtime Sanders operative who is now consulting for Khanna. Over the last week, the California representative has been on what he is calling an "new economic patriotism tour" through Pennsylvania, holding events in counties Trump carried like Erie, Luzerne and Cambria "There is a great desire for a bold, progressive vision that is going to call out an unfair and rigged political and economic system," he told POLITICO. But the test, Khanna argued, is making that vision work "not just in the Bay Area, not just in Michigan, not just in progressive areas, but in places like Pennsylvania." Khanna has endorsed dozens of candidates up and down the ballot this year, wading into some of the most fraught Democratic House, Senate and gubernatorial primaries in the country. That widespread involvement has produced a mixed track record with some high-profile losses, including Graham Platner’s disgraced exit from Maine’s Senate primary and Tom Steyer’s expensive loss in the California governor’s race. In the case of Platner, Khanna and Sanders endorsed the Maine progressive, while Ocasio-Cortez, notably, stayed out of the race altogether. Khanna also has backed candidates against the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and establishment. For example, Khanna-endorsed progressive Matt Dunlap in Maine’s 2nd Congressional District successfully defeated the DCCC’s preferred candidate. “There’s a difference between being a progressive in policies and being a progressive in action,” said Uygur. “And action requires you challenging the system, challenging the establishment. On those grounds, it’s not close. Ro Khanna is head and shoulders above every other Democrat.”
articles.headline: Bernie Sanders’ circle is pretty clear on who his successor will be

articles.body: Cori Bush’s 2024 primary loss to Wesley Bell was heralded as a major defeat for the insurgent progressive movement. Now, their rematch for Missouri’s 1st District two years later comes at a time when Bush and her allies seem to be winning the battle for the future of the Democratic Party. The dueling factions in St. Louis highlight the growing tension over not just the domestic ideological divide in the Democratic Party, but the party’s — and country’s — stance on the U.S.'s longrunning relationship with Israel. The former representative was among the first sitting members of Congress to call Israel's actions in Gaza a "genocide" — and now she's betting that her progressive bonafides and her criticism of the top U.S. ally will boost her to victory with the same electorate that punished her last cycle. “One of us is of the people, by the people and for the people,” Bush said in a recent interview. “The other one is paid for by AIPAC. That's the difference.” Like two years ago, a group aligned with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee is the largest outside spender in the race. The organization’s super PAC, United Democracy Project, has spent at least $2.1 million on advertising in the primary, according to ad tracking firm AdImpact. Roughly half of all adults who identify as Democrats believe that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians, according to a July AP-NORC poll , an accusation that some human rights organizations have made but both the Israeli and American governments strongly deny. And from Colorado to New York, several progressives have already tapped into voters' frustrations with party leadership and successfully wielded their criticism of Israel's government in order to win. St. Louis is only one of several races on Tuesday testing the Democratic Party’s establishment: voters will also hit the polls in Michigan to cast their ballots for the progressive, Abdul El-Sayed, or the moderate Rep. Haley Stevens for an open Senate seat. That race has also become a check for voters’ opposition to AIPAC. And some potential 2028 Democratic contenders have already sworn off accepting funding from AIPAC, another sign of the growing unwillingness to be aligned with the organization. AIPAC and some Democrats have hit back, saying its critics within the Democratic Party have increasingly made the party inhospitable to those generally supportive of Israel. In response to requests for comment, AIPAC shared a series of ads knocking Bush for her missed votes and her criticism of the Biden administration and former Vice President Kamala Harris’s 2024 presidential bid. (In a recent debate, Bush claimed Bell delayed his endorsement of Harris, but both endorsed the former vice president on July 21, 2024 , the same day she announced her candidacy.) Bell unseated Bush two years ago with heavy financial backing from AIPAC, the country’s preeminent pro-Israel lobby. They’ve once again spent heavily on his behalf, and this time, he also comes into the race with establishment support — including endorsements from House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and the Congressional Black Caucus PAC. Bell and his allies have absolutely swamped Bush on the airwaves this year. In addition to UDP’s $2.1 million in ad spending, Bell’s campaign has followed closely behind at over $2 million, according to AdImpact, with over $700,000 more from another super PAC called New Democrat Majority. Bush, meanwhile, has spent less than $200,000, according to the ad tracker. She boasts the backing of a progressive coalition that includes the Democratic Socialists of America, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and fellow "Squad" member Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.). Bell has brushed aside the attacks that he’s being bolstered by AIPAC money. “I think we all can agree that there's too much money in politics, and I'm a vocal and public supporter of campaign finance reform,” Bell said in an interview. “What I'm not a fan of or a supporter of is singling out certain Americans and saying that they should not participate in our democratic process. That is where I would absolutely draw the line.” Bell added that the difference between himself and Bush is that he can offer both support and criticism of allies. “While I’m not the biggest fan of [Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu], I still believe that we have to stand with our allies,” Bell said. “That doesn't mean we're not going to disagree at times with our allies.” Bell’s and Bush’s showdown in 2024 was arguably the biggest ideological battlefield for the party that year, outside of the discontent surrounding Biden and then Harris’ presidential bids from progressives critical of Israel. But two years later, it is just one of many fights that has sprawled across the country. Progressive candidates have been racking up primary victories against establishment figures in a trend that some are calling the “Mamdani effect” after democratic socialist New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani took down Andrew Cuomo in both the 2025 primary and general elections. Still, this year’s St. Louis rematch isn’t quite the marquee fight it was in 2024. Spending has trended down: Collectively nearly $20 million was dropped on the 2024 contest on advertising, according to AdImpact. That’s roughly four times more than this year’s total. Usamah Andrabi, spokesperson for Justice Democrats, the progressive group that endorsed Bush earlier this cycle, attributed the broader, nationwide ideological fight to a base that has been “pushed to the edge of desperation by the Democratic Party itself.” “The Democratic Party’s base woke up in January 2025 realizing that their party's establishment was unfit, unprepared and frankly unwilling to fight back against Donald Trump and Republican extremists with the urgency the moment demanded,” Andrabi said. Now, as St. Louis voters head to the polls on Tuesday, Bush cast the eventual outcome in dire terms. “What is at stake,” Bush said, “is the affordability and the peace of every single person in this country.”
articles.headline: Democrats’ stance on Israel takes center stage in Bush-Bell rematch in St. Louis

articles.body: (ACN) Bombers de Barcelona ha evacuat de forma preventiva els treballadors de l’empresa Bonfred, SA , ubicada al polígon Mercabarna, a causa d’una fuita d’amoníac que no ha causat ferits . L’avís s’ha rebut a les 0.14 h a través del telèfon d’emergències 112 i fins al punt s’hi han mobilitzat 11 dotacions del cos. Els efectius han aturat la fuita i l’han poguda controlar . Posteriorment han ventilat la nau de la companyia, que es dedica a la logística alimentària i a l’emmagatzematge frigorífic. Arran del succés, Protecció Civil ha activat el pla Procicat i l’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha posat en fase d’alerta el seu Pla d’Actuació d’Emergència Municipal. Tots dos dispositius ja s’han desactivat . Fuita a la sala de màquines En arribar al lloc dels fets, Bombers de Barcelona ha confirmat que la fuita s’havia originat a la sala de màquines de la nau i que el producte s’estava emetent a través de les canonades exteriors situades a la part superior de l’edifici. Els serveis d’emergència han aconseguit aturar l’emissió de producte i, posteriorment, han dut a terme tasques de ventilació per garantir la seguretat de les instal·lacions. El Sistema d’Emergències Mèdiques (SEM) també ha mobilitzat una unitat fins al lloc, tot i que finalment no ha estat necessària cap assistència, ja que no hi ha hagut cap persona ferida ni intoxicada .
articles.headline: Evacuada una empresa de Mercabarna per una fuita d’amoníac ja controlada que no ha causat ferits

articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) Barcelona ha perdut una de cada quatre merceries i drogueries entre l’any 2016 i el 2024, i també un 30 % de les sabateries i negocis de pell , segons els censos municipals de locals comercials. Les dades il·lustren el retrocés del comerç tradicional i al detall , que en l’àmbit de l’alimentació també es veu en negocis com les peixateries —n’han tancat 141 en aquests vuit anys, quasi el 25 %—, les botigues d’ous i aviram —un 15 % menys— i fins i tot les carnisseries —un 10 % menys. Per fer front a aquesta situació, l’alcalde, Jaume Collboni, va plantejar recentment regular els lloguers comercials i un fons per comprar locals emblemàtics “en risc” . També et pot interessar La centenària Perfumeria del Bonsuccés: “La clau és ser diferent o ser vulgar com la Coca-Cola” Marta de San Nicolás Montse Llorens 3 minuts de lectura Merceries en perill d’extinció Les merceries han desaparegut a poc a poc de la ciutat i ara n’hi ha menys de 200. El darrer tancament ha estat el de la històrica merceria Tarragona , que va abaixar la persiana després de 109 anys al barri de Gràcia. Entre els qui encara resisteixen hi ha el Ramon Martínez Perelló, tercera generació de la Merceria Perelló . El seu negoci resisteix “ adaptant-se de forma camaleònica al client ”, però té dubtes que la quarta generació segueixi el llegat. “Abans hi havia una merceria cada tres cantonades, ara n’hi ha una cada tres barris”, apunta Perelló. Entre les causes d’aquest declivi, reconeix que els basars xinesos els han fet mal perquè ofereixen molts dels seus productes, tot i que “amb una qualitat inferior i un servei d’assistència del qual no es poden fer càrrec”. També et pot interessar Barcelona finalitzarà la reforma de tots els mercats municipals d’aquí a cinc anys Arnau Vaqué Marta Casals Torres 1 minut de lectura Desaparició d’altres negocis tradicionals Les merceries no són els únics negocis que han anat desapareixent en els últims anys. Les sabateries i els negocis de pell viuen una situació molt semblant. En menys d’una dècada han tancat almenys 250 establiments , un 30 % dels que hi havia el 2016. El cas de les drogueries i les perfumeries no és una excepció i també han abaixat la persiana un 25 % dels negocis que hi havia el 2016. L’alimentació dels barcelonins també ha canviat i ara el més habitual és comprar als supermercats. Com a conseqüència d’aquest canvi d’hàbits, s’han perdut pràcticament una de cada quatre peixateries , un 15 % de les botigues d’ous i aviram i un 10 % de les carnisseries. Mesures per protegir el comerç Pròsper Puig, president de la Fundació Barcelona Comerç i expropietari de la històrica Cansaladeria Puig , assumeix que el tancament del negoci tradicional és una realitat que volen combatre , tot i que defensa que els eixos comercials mantenen una fortalesa important . Sobre la proposta feta recentment per l’alcalde Collboni de regular lloguers comercials i comprar locals emblemàtics “en risc”, Puig considera que veu és difícil la protecció del comerç històric, però es poden fer moltes coses. Per la seva banda, Perelló demana no només mesures econòmiques, sinó també un relaxament de les normatives municipals (retolació, il·luminació, accés adaptat, regulació laboral, etc., segons enumera): “Fan que cada vegada ens sigui més complicat tirar endavant el negoci”. També et pot interessar El primer supermercat de tot Catalunya sobreviu a Sant Martí 67 anys després: “Va ser revolucionari” Ester Magdaleno 2 minuts de lectura Dinamisme comercial barceloní Les dades d’obertura i tancament d’establiments s’han de posar en un context de dinamisme comercial a Barcelona. Actualment hi ha 61.875 locals actius a la ciutat, un increment d’un 2,6 % (1.500 negocis) respecte del 2016. En aquest sentit, la reculada dels tradicionals no es pot imputar en cap cas a una davallada del volum de negocis. A més, hi ha alguns creixements comercials que sobresurten, com l’obertura sostinguda d’establiments de gimnàs i fitnes , dels quals la ciutat té un terç més que el 2022: de 367 locals s’ha passat a 486 en tan sols dos anys (no es pot comparar amb el 2016 perquè estaven agrupats gimnasos i equipaments esportius). També es pot inferir l’impacte del comerç electrònic en l’augment de les activitats d’emmagatzematge, amb un creixement espectacular del 44 %, 800 punts a la ciutat en dos anys, de 1.684 a 2.419.

articles.body: La final del Mundial 2030 s’allunya del Camp Nou de forma momentània, ja que The Times assegura que el president de la FIFA , Gianni Infantino , hauria ofert el partit a la Federació Marroquina , que acolliria la final al futur estadi Hassan II de Casablanca . Una reacció directa al boicot que fa uns dies va anunciar la UEFA al president de la FIFA per la seva voluntat de privatitzar aquesta cita mundialista. D’aquesta manera, aquest moviment també respondria a la voluntat d’ Infantino de reforçar els suports de les federacions africanes en un moment de forta pressió interna. També et pot interessar Jaume Collboni i la final del Mundial 2030 a Barcelona: “Competim, com sempre, amb Madrid” Roger Matamoros i Aparicio 2 minuts de lectura Un gir inesperat que colpeja la Federació Espanyola de Futbol Si aquesta opció acabés prosperant, Espanya es quedaria sense el partit més important del torneig malgrat comptar amb dos dels grans candidats a acollir-lo: el renovat Camp Nou i el Santiago Bernabéu . articles.body: (EFE) Més afectacions aquest dimecres a l’aeroport del Prat a causa de la vaga indefinida del personal de terra, facturació i embarcament de Groundforce . Al llarg d’aquesta segona jornada d’aturada, s’han cancel·lat 18 vols entre viatges d’anada i tornada. Aquest nombre d’afectacions s’afegeix a la vintena de suspensions que es van comptabilitzar dimarts en el primer dia de vaga . Per ara, no s’han produït avenços en les negociacions , segons han comunicat des de la CGT, el sindicat que convoca l’aturada. També et pot interessar Alguns vols cancel·lats i retards a l’aeroport de Barcelona per la vaga de personal de terra Jessica Moreno Cusac 2 minuts de lectura Seguiment “molt alt” La CGT és el sindicat majoritari, amb més d’un terç de la representació al comitè d’empresa. En declaracions a EFE, la portaveu del comitè de vaga, Esther García, ha assegurat que el seguiment de la mobilització continua sent “molt alt” entre els 1.179 treballadors de la companyia, que presta servei a aerolínies com Air Europa, Lufthansa, Air France, KLM, Qatar Airways o Etihad Airways. També et pot interessar Quins són els drets dels passatgers afectats per la vaga a l’aeroport de Barcelona? Segons el sindicat, la decisió d’anar a vaga respon a la inacció de la direcció davant el “greu deteriorament” de la prevenció de riscos i les condicions de salut laboral a la base. articles.body: Un incendi de grans flames ha calcinat tres contenidors al barri del Guinardó . El foc s’ha produït a les tres de la matinada a l’altura del número 74 del carrer del Segle XX . Una dotació de Bombers s’ha traslladat al lloc del fets i ha sufocat l’incendi de manera ràpida, com es pot veure al vídeo enregistrat per una veïna al mateix carrer. Aquest no és el primer ensurt dels veïns del Guinardó aquest estiu a causa de la crema de contenidors. El 16 de juliol tres contenidors van quedar completament calcinats a la rambla de la Muntanya , a pocs carrers d’on ha passat l’incendi d’aquesta matinada. articles.body: El Banc dels Aliments recorda que “ la necessitat d’aliments no fa vacances ” i fa un crida a seguir rebent donacions també durant el mes d’agost, quan baixa la intensitat dels donatius. De fet, l’entitat alerta que els mesos d’estiu poden ser especialment complexos per a les llars amb menys recursos perquè, per exemple, les escoles i els menjadors escolars estan tancats i, per tant, els infants estan més hores a casa . La previsió del Banc dels Aliments de Barcelona és distribuir al voltant d’ un milió de quilos d’aliments durant l’agost d’aquest 2026 a través de la xarxa d’entitats socials. La xifra és una estimació feta a partir de l’activitat del 2025. En total, durant l’any passat va distribuir 12.671.410 kg d’aliments, una mitjana aproximada d’ 1.056.000 kg cada mes. “Les persones i famílies que tenen dificultats per arribar a final de mes les continuen tenint durant l’estiu. Per això és important que la solidaritat s mantingui els 12 mesos de l’any” Elisabet Viladomiu, directora del Banc dels Aliments de Barcelona També et pot interessar Baixen lleugerament les donacions del Gran Recapte del Banc dels Aliments Àngels Molina Marta Casals Torres 1 minut de lectura Donacions per internet La vicepresidenta del Banc dels Aliments, Roser Brutau , ha explicat a betevé que des de l’entitat s’ha fet “un gran esforç ” perquè totes les persones que s’abasteixen de centres com menjadors o centres escolars, que ara estan tancats, puguin tenir aliments durant les vacances. “A hores d’ara ja hem repartit més d’1,5 milions de quilos d’aliments “, afirma Brutau. L’entitat també explica que durant les vacances acostumen a baixar les campanyes de recollida organitzades per escoles, empreses i altres entitats, així com la mobilització ciutadana. Per això recorda a la ciutadania que es poden fer donacions puntuals o periòdiques a través del web del Banc dels Aliments de Barcelona . En aquest sentit, diu que les aportacions de diners permeten adaptar les compres a les necessites de les entitats socials i garantir una distribució d’aliments més estable al llarg de l’any. I, en qualsevol dels casos, també recorda que tot tipus d’aportació, independentment de l’import , contribueix a garantir que l’ajuda alimentària arribi a les persones que ho necessitem. “Anem per bon camí, però esperem que la ciutadania ens ajudi i pugui contribuir amb donacions”, reclama Brutau. articles.body: Aleksander Sekulic ha estat presentat oficialment com a entrenador del Barça de bàsquet aquest dimecres, amb el repte de rellançar un projecte que busca recuperar protagonisme tant a la Lliga Endesa com a l’ Eurolliga . El tècnic eslovè, que inicia etapa a la banqueta blaugrana, ha deixat clar quin ha de ser el segell del seu equip: “Una proposta més intensa, física i dinàmica que la de les darreres temporades” . En aquest sentit, ha assegurat que vol que els aficionats reconeguin l’estil de joc del seu equip i que treballarà per consolidar una identitat pròpia, amb un joc dinàmic, físic i més ràpid que el de la temporada passada . Alhora, ha assumit l’exigència que comporta dirigir el club blaugrana i ha afirmat que espera superar les expectatives d’un club tan gran com el Barça . També et pot interessar El Barça de bàsquet oficialitza l’arribada de Xevi Pujol per liderar el nou projecte Àlex Masana 1 minut de lectura L’eslovè vol rejovenir la plantilla Durant la presentació, Sekulic també ha explicat que la renovació de la plantilla respon a la voluntat de construir un equip amb més marge de creixement. “Volem tenir un equip més jove per canviar una mica el que ha passat en les últimes temporades. Hi ha alguns jugadors que no tenen experiència a l’Eurolliga, però crec que tots els fitxatges que hem fet són capaços d’adaptar-se al nostre estil de joc” , ha destacat. Tot i això, l’entrenador ha demanat paciència amb el procés d’adaptació, ja que considera que el grup necessitarà més temps del que és habitual “per raons òbvies”, tot i mostrar-se convençut del projecte: “Tenim talent i hem de treballar-lo perquè jugui com nosaltres volem” .

articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El president d’ERC, Oriol Junqueras, ha proposat aquest dimecres un gran acord perquè la conselleria d’Educació estigui liderada per un equip d’experts durant 12 anys i tingui pressupostos estables. En una entrevista a Catalunya Ràdio, Junqueras ha assenyalat: “Té poc sentit que hi hagi una nova llei educativa cada legislatura o canviar de conseller cada any”. La proposta ha estat rebatuda per USTEC , el sindicat educatiu majoritari. La portaveu, Iolanda Segura , ha dit: “Més que noves fórmules o invents , cal que s’escolti la comunitat educativa ”. Tot, en un context en què hi ha convocada una vaga el primer dia de curs, el 8 de setembre . També et pot interessar El curs escolar començarà el 8 de setembre els pròxims tres anys Jessica Moreno Cusac 1 minut de lectura “Persones solvents i reconegudes” El líder d’Esquerra creu que aquest grup hauria d’estar integrat per “persones solvents i reconegudes” que puguin garantir una actuació a llarg termini. Així, fa una crida a partits polítics i agents socials per consensuar les prioritats i donar així “tranquil·litat d’esperit i una certa constància” al sector. Al seu torn, Segura considera que la diagnosi d’Educació ja es troba consensuada amb els grups polítics i agents socials. En tot cas, la portaveu d’USTEC ha puntualitzat que no es pot pronunciar del tot fins que no es pugui aprofundir detalladament en la proposta. I, tal com ja va passar en el Mundial de Singapur l’any 2025 , Iris Tió s’ha tornat a penjar sis medalles. En aquesta ocasió, han estat un or, quatre plates i un bronze . L’última actuació ha estat aquest dimecres, en què el conjunt espanyol ha pujat al segon graó del podi en la rutina d’equip acrobàtic . articles.body: Protecció Civil de la Generalitat ha activat dimecres al migdia el pla especial d’emergències per inundacions de Catalunya (l’ Inuncat ) en fase d’alerta per la previsió de tempestes fortes dijous, 6 d’agost, entre la tarda i el vespre. L’Inuncat s’ha activat seguint els avisos de perill per pluja intensa i abundant emesos pel Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya . Les tempestes també es preveu que puguin descarregar amb energia a l’entorn metropolità de Barcelona , sobretot al prelitoral. Els xàfecs arribaran posteriorment a la costa i a la mateixa ciutat de Barcelona, tot i que ja més desgastats. També et pot interessar Aparat elèctric: com actuar en cas de veure’ns sorpresos per una tempesta Manel Cascante Torrella 4 minuts de lectura Avisos d’intensitat de precipitació de més de 40 litres en 30 minuts en alguns sectors de Catalunya El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha emès un avís per possible superació del llindar de perill per intensitat de pluja i també per acumulació de pluja en algunes comarques. L’avís per intensitat de pluja abraça bona part de Catalunya , sobretot les comarques del nord-est, la Catalunya central i el prelitoral central. Es tracta d’un avís de perill de grau (4/6) per la possibilitat que es recullin més de 40 litres en tan sols 30 minuts (fins a un 30 % de probabilitat que així sigui). L’avís d’intensitat és de grau baix (1/6) al Barcelonès . Això indica que la probabilitat que caiguin més de 20 litres en 30 minuts és de fins al 30 %. El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha actualitzat l'avís de situació meteorològica de perill ( #avisosSMP ) per intensitat de pluja Dj. de 14:00 h a Dv. 20:00 h Llindar: > 40 mm / 30 minuts Grau de perill màxim: 4/6 *Hora local (h) = TU +2 pic.twitter.com/0Waz6LxWSn — Meteocat (@meteocat) August 5, 2026 L’avís de perill d’acumulació de precipitació fa referència a la possibilitat que caiguin més de 60 litres en només tres hores. Es tracta d’un avís de grau moderat que abraça les comarques del prelitoral, l’interior i dels Pirineus i Prepirineu orientals . És d’un 2/6, fet que indica que hi ha entre un 30 i un 70 % de probabilitat que se superi aquest llindar establert. El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha emès un avís de situació meteorològica de perill ( #avisosSMP ) per intensitat de pluja en 3 hores Dj. de 14:00 a 20:00 h Llindar: > 60 mm / 3 hores Grau de perill màxim: 2/6 *Hora local (h) = TU +2 pic.twitter.com/WruHT2tAbO — Meteocat (@meteocat) August 5, 2026 El Meteocat avisa que els xàfecs aniran acompanyats de tempestes i localment de fenòmens de temps violent, sobretot ratxes de vent molt fortes i de pedra . Les tempestes seran fortes al prelitoral central i arribaran posteriorment a Barcelona El cel clar del matí de dijous no ens ha de fer abaixar la guàrdia , ja que la presència d’una mica d’aire fred en altura afavorirà el creixement de les nuvolades i la formació de nuclis de tempesta actius a partir del migdia. Les tempestes aniran guanyant extensió als Pirineus a partir del migdia , alhora que s ‘aniran movent gradualment de nord cap a sud . Afectaran amb forta intensitat les comarques interiors al llarg de la tarda i tot indica que arribaran al prelitoral barceloní a partir de mitja tarda. Entre les 18 i les 20 h aproximadament afectaran la plana vallesana , i entre les 20 i les 21 o 22 h podrien afectar la mateixa línia costanera situada entre la Selva i el Baix Penedès. Plourà gaire a Barcelona? Les tempestes perdran empenta en arribar al litoral , tot i que en algunes zones encara podrien arribar prou actives com per descarregar xàfecs forts. Convé tenir present que es tracta d’una situació incerta associada a les tempestes , que acostumen a tenir una distribució irregular. A Barcelona tot fa pensar, ara per ara, que no hi plourà gaire , tot i que cap a Collserola o la part nord, prop del Besòs, es podrien recollir més de 10 litres per metre quadrat. En qualsevol cas, serà necessari fer un seguiment acurat del pronòstic al llarg de les properes hores . Protecció Civil demana extremar la prudència, sobretot pel que fa als desplaçaments en vehicles, i en les activitats que es facin a l’aire lliure. Es recomana: Evitar aparcar en rieres o punts inundables. No travessar mai rius, rieres ni zones negades, ni a peu ni amb vehicle. Reduir la mobilitat en cas de precipitacions intenses. articles.body: Kerolin Nicoli ja llueix els colors blaugrana. I ho ha fa amb un somriure d’orella a orella: “Quan em va trucar el Barça no m’ho podria creure. Quan vaig veure que la cosa ja era seriosament, vaig pensar que no podia perdre l’oportunitat”, ha dit. La davantera brasilera, que arriba procedent del Manchester City , ha assegurat que jugar al club blaugrana la farà millor jugadora i l’ajudarà a créixer per arribar a ser la millor futbolista del planteta. El Barça ha pagat 1,2 milions d’euros per la jugadora, que es converteix així en la futbolista per la qual el club blaugrana ha pagat més en tota la història. Ella entoma el repte i no s’espanta: “Estic molt agraïda per l’aposta que ha fet el club i en el futur demostraré per què m’ha fitxat”. Els ídols de Kerolin Nicoli Kerolin Nicoli, de 26 anys , és nascuda al Brasil, a Sao Paulo . I, com no podia ser d’una altra manera, té referents brasilers. “De petita, veia jugar a Neymar i Ronaldinho amb el Barça i ara formo part del club. És un somni”, ha sentenciat. A Nicoli també li han preguntat per les jugadores amb qui vol jugar de la plantilla culer i s’ha mullat: Pajor ,  Aitana, Vicky, Patri i Sydney . “I també vull conèixer la Kika , perquè té pinta que és molt divertida”, ha afegit amb un somriure.
